prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this system, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: I keep the single-achievement prize for magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. After the full exchange I still find it the clearest example on the shortlist of what I look for: a simple, general mechanism (two lattices with a small relative twist produce a moire superlattice, and the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model puts nearly flat bands at a specific angle) that made a quantitative prediction, followed by an experiment that found more than was asked for. The flat-band structure is understood in a controlled way, and what is established is the phenomenology: correlated insulators and superconducting domes at the magic angle, reproduced by many independent groups with transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy, and extended to twisted TMDs and fractional Chern insulators. The citation should be limited to the prediction of the flat bands and the observed phases, and say nothing about the pairing mechanism. The three-person allocation (Bistritzer and MacDonald for the prediction, Jarillo-Herrero for the decisive experimental discovery) follows the same rule we use for large experimental teams: credit the conceptual origin and the leader of the decisive experiment, and record in the committee's reasoning that the student-led and parallel work (Cao, Dean, Kim, Young, Efetov, Ashoori) is part of the same history.
statement.case_against: The two weaknesses that remain are maturity and attribution, and round 1 did not remove either. Eight years is short, the pairing mechanism and the nature of several correlated states are open, and Johansson and Danielsson make a fair argument that waiting a few years would cost little. Attribution is imperfect because Yuan Cao and other early experimental groups cannot be named under the three-person limit, and the earlier twist-angle theory of Lopes dos Santos and collaborators is a priority question I cannot resolve from the material. Optical lattice clocks (B042) have a cleaner two-name attribution, a settled interpretation and independent reproduction across several national laboratories, so a member who weights maturity above novelty of mechanism can reasonably prefer them. I regard B042 as a defensible and mature prize, and I would not treat it as a poor outcome.

responses.point: Pearce asked what in the superconducting mechanism could change in the next few years, and whether my reservation about the clocks concerns timing, the 2005 and 2012 overlap, or the kind of result.
responses.response: On the mechanism: the debate is between phonon-mediated and purely electronic pairing, and between competing pictures of the correlated insulators (strong-coupling, Wannier-orbital and Hartree-Fock-type descriptions). Better samples, tunnelling spectroscopy and twist-angle-controlled devices could favour one picture. None of that would remove the phases, the flat-band prediction or the existence of the platform. What can change is the explanation, not the observation, and so a citation limited to the prediction and the observed phases is robust to any outcome. That is the answer to whether it is too early. On the clocks, my reservation is the kind of result: I read them as a decisive performance advance on a line the committee has honoured twice, not as a new mechanism. It is not about timing and not mainly about overlap, and I accept that Katori's magic-wavelength condition is a clean idea, which is why I rank B042 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Kroll asks whether the committee gains by waiting on twisted bilayers when the clock case is already complete, and argues that reaching 1e-18 required new understanding of blackbody, collisional and tunnelling shifts.
responses.response: I accept that the clock case is complete today and that the magic-wavelength condition is a general criterion. My answer on waiting is that the cost depends on which robust result we reward. The flat-band prediction and the observed phases will not be undone by a later understanding of pairing, while the case for B019 is time-sensitive in another way: the credit chain is clearer now than it will be once the follow-on literature obscures who did what. I also take your point that the clock is not a mere refinement, since controlling the systematics at 1e-18 is physics in its own right. We differ on whether that adds up to a new regime or to the next step on the 2005 and 2012 line. I do not claim to have shown you wrong on that, and if the committee settles on B042 I will support Katori and Ye with a citation built on the lattice-clock concept, as you propose.

responses.point: Johansson does not accept that the open superconductivity mechanism is only a timing issue, and thinks it favours waiting a few years.
responses.response: I agree it is more than a calendar matter, which is why I will not let the citation touch the mechanism. But the standard we have applied is whether the discovered phenomenon is robust and reproduced, not whether its microscopic origin is settled. Phenomena whose explanation lagged the observation have been honoured before. I would also point out that the question is not symmetric: B042 also rests on a still-incomplete outlook, since the redefinition of the second has not happened and you correctly say the citation should avoid it. Neither candidate is free of loose ends, and I think the loose end on B019 is the one that does not affect what we would be crediting. If you still prefer to wait, I ask that you say whether you would object to B019 as a second choice behind B042, since your first alternative is already B019.

responses.point: Eriksson asks whether the KPZ credit chain (Kardar and Zhang for the equation, Takeuchi for the experiment, exact-solution community omitted) is as thin as my own attribution note suggests, and defers on B037.
responses.response: It is thin in exactly the way my own note says. KPZ universality is a real and general result, and Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments are the clearest confirmation of the exact scaling functions. But the exact solutions that fixed the distributions (Johansson, Prahofer and Spohn, Sasamoto and Spohn, Amir, Corwin and Quastel, Calabrese and Le Doussal) are what made the experimental test sharp, and none of them can be named in a three-person allocation that also credits Kardar and Zhang. With a single first place in the whole committee and no supporter after round 1, I now treat B037 as a strong subject for a later year and not as a configuration I can defend today. I therefore keep it only as a ballot alternative. On two-part prizes, I agree with you that pairing B019 with a more mature candidate is attractive in principle, but the three-person limit makes it impossible here: B019 alone uses three names.

responses.point: Olsson asks that the committee record the reproduction record in its reasoning, notes that the allocation is clean only at the level of group leadership, and keeps B042 as a mature alternative while asking what Ye's clocks add that is original.
responses.response: I agree and I will gladly state the reproduction record as part of the reasoning: independent observations of correlated insulators and superconductivity in several laboratories, with different probes, and with the known caveat that the results depend on twist-angle control and sample quality. I also accept your qualification that the credit is clean only at the group-leadership level; the committee record should say that Yuan Cao and the student team are part of the discovery. On your question about Ye, I side with Kroll and Lindroth that the realisation at record accuracy and stability is more than superior execution, though I still read Katori's proposal and first demonstration as the originating step. That is the main reason B042 is my alternative and not my first choice, and also the reason I would accept it without difficulty.

responses.point: Danielsson would not oppose a condensed-matter prize this year but would want a few more years of settled interpretation before placing B019 above an observational discovery such as IceCube.
responses.response: I respect the preference for a new window on nature, and I agree that the diffuse neutrino flux is secure. My difficulty with B032 is not the flux but the pairing of credit: I do not have the information to decide whether Spiering's Baikal and DUMAND-era role is as decisive as Halzen's, and you yourself leave that to the expert reports. Without that, I cannot place B032 above a case where a prediction and the first experiment are both identifiable. On interpretation, our standards are not far apart: you would word the IceCube citation around the flux, not around the 3-4 sigma sources, and I would word B019 around the phases, not the pairing. On those terms I do not think the flux is better settled than the flat-band physics.

uncertainties: Whether the earlier twist-angle continuum-model work of Lopes dos Santos and collaborators should change the credited theory names; I cannot verify this from the material provided.
Whether the omission of Yuan Cao and other early experimental groups can be handled by the citation and the committee record alone, or whether it is a defect that should make the committee wait.
Whether the committee will accept that the open pairing mechanism does not bear on a prize for the prediction and the observed phases.
Whether the committee will prefer B042 on maturity and attribution grounds, in which case I would support Katori and Ye with a citation limited to the lattice-clock concept and its realisation.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent from my profile for MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, or for the alternative names (Katori, Ye; Takeuchi, Kardar, Zhang). I know of no collaboration, supervision or institutional tie to any of them. I share the Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson (Chalmers), but none of them is a credited candidate in my configuration. I note that my opening first choice was B037, and that I have moved away from it because of the attribution problem and the lack of support.
